methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Tech Briefs: Virginia Tech research team gets $20 million grant for cloud-based semiconductor lab
signals.signal_reading: A $20M federal grant for cloud-based semiconductor research at Virginia Tech signals deep capability building, but the cloud-based delivery model could enable distributed access if Virginia leverages it beyond the Blacksburg hub to train workforce across regions.

signals.title: Roanoke College launches WorkAI Lab to prepare leaders for new era of technology - roanoke.edu
signals.signal_reading: Roanoke College's WorkAI Lab represents deliberate institutional capacity-building in a non-metro region, creating potential peer networks for AI fluency outside traditional tech corridors—a critical signal for distributed depth if sustained beyond initial launch.

signals.title: Norfolk native brings free AI workshops to Hampton Roads to close the technology gap - WTKR
signals.signal_reading: Free community AI workshops in Hampton Roads demonstrate grassroots capability distribution through accessible education, directly counteracting the concentration dynamic by building local fluency networks independent of elite institutional gatekeepers.

signals.title: Internet provider ZiTel approved to finish broadband deployment work in Patrick, Franklin, Henry counties
signals.signal_reading: Broadband deployment completion in Patrick, Franklin, and Henry counties enables platform-based AI access in historically underserved Southside, but infrastructure alone without training programs signals shallow adoption rather than deep capability building.

signals.title: In the data center capital of the world, residents ask who the AI boom is helping - nbcnews.com
signals.signal_reading: Residents questioning who benefits from NoVA's data center boom reveals that physical AI infrastructure concentration doesn't translate to distributed economic opportunity or local capability—infrastructure without inclusion reinforces rather than bridges divides.
